opportunities.title: Commercial Kitchen Exhaust (Hood) Cleaning Service
opportunities.idea: Deep-clean grease from commercial kitchen exhaust hoods, ducts & fans for restaurants, hotels, cafeterias, cloud kitchens in Mumbai/Bangalore. Compliance-mandated recurring service.

scorecard.working_capital: 9/10 (Prepaid quarterly AMC or payment upon job completion. Zero inventory loss.)
scorecard.vendor_lockin: 9/10 (Open commoditized degreasers, portable 3500 PSI pressure washers, no OEM lockout.)
scorecard.labor_friction: 7/10 (Overnight 11pm-4am shifts; mitigated by paying 25% performance commission per hood).
scorecard.regulatory_moat: 9/10 (Mandatory NFPA-96 / local fire-safety compliance; involuntary commercial demand).
scorecard.capital_velocity: 10/10 (₹5–15L all-in capex; positive EBITDA from Month 1-2 with 15 accounts).

why_passes: Involuntary Legal Demand: Commercial kitchens are legally required under fire-safety codes to degrease exhaust hoods quarterly to prevent grease fires.
High Gross Margin: Standard hood clean is ₹3,000–₹15,000 per kitchen; chemical and consumable cost is under ₹800/job (65–75% gross margin).
Fast Cash Breakeven: A 2-man crew can service 2 hoods per night (₹10,000/night revenue). 20 recurring restaurant locations generate ₹3.5–4.5L/month top-line.
unit_economics: Initial Capex: ₹5.5L – 12L (Commercial hot-water pressure washer, rotary duct brushes, wet vac, scaffolding, PPE, used utility vehicle).
Monthly Revenue (30 restaurants, quarterly cleans): ₹4.5L – 6.0L/month including filter exchange upsells.
Monthly EBITDA: 28% – 42% (₹1.3L – 2.4L/month net operating cash flow).
watchouts: Avoid scattered geography: 40+ accounts must be within a 15km micro-market radius (e.g. Bandra-BKC-Andheri in Mumbai, or Indiranagar-Koramangala-HSR in BLR) to prevent traffic from destroying route profitability.
Insurance Trap: General liability policies do not cover grease fires occurring after technicians leave. Must obtain specialized completed-operations fire coverage.

opportunities.notes: Local medical-equipment rental depot + home-ICU bundle (5L/10L oxygen concentrators, BiPAP/CPAP, ICU beds, monitors, ventilators) in one metro, Bangalore-first. NOT a marketplace play — moat is trusted hospital/pulmonologist/discharge-coordinator referrals, 2-hr delivery SLA, 65-75% fleet utilization, sanitized ISO-standard fleet. Bangalore easiest ops (dense demand, better digital lead capture). Critical trap: full home-health with employed nurses destroys margins — Portea -6.88% EBITDA, Emoha -48.86%; a scoped local rental operator can hit positive EBITDA vs loss-making growth platforms. Delhi with a dedicated 3-5 hospital referral wedge. WATCH-OUTS: fragmented + price-transparent market (dozens of local suppliers, hospital vendor lists); sub-50% utilization kills economics; high-ticket ventilators carry downtime + clinical liability; medical-device licensing + infection-control SOPs; needs 7-15 day min rental term + refundable deposits + KYC/prescription.
